title: Proportion of population with positive out-of-pocket household expenditures on health exceeding 40 per cent of household discretionary budget
graph_title: Out-of-pocket health expenditure per capita, PPP
national_indicator_available: Out-of-pocket health expenditure per capita, PPP
national_indicator_description: As noted in the [Forward Looking Joint Health Sector Review Report for Fiscal Year 2023/2024](https://www.moh.gov.rw/index.php?eID=dumpFile&t=f&f=70771&token=f73c868b77d22d7833d7762c29cde46f7ec0b4b3), this indicator is among the SDG indicators not currently monitored by the Ministry of Health. Due to a lack of comparable timeseries data, this indicator uses out-of-pocket health expenditure per capita as a proxy for the proportion of the population with positive out-of-pocket household expenditures on health exceeding 40 per cent of household discretionary budget.
computation_definitions: Out-of-pocket household expenditure on health includes any expenditure incurred at the time-of-service use to get any type of care (promotive, preventive, curative, rehabilitative, palliative, or long-term care) including all medicines, vaccines and other pharmaceutical preparations as well as all health products, from any type of provider and for all members of the household. It is financed by a household’s income (including remittances), savings or loans but do not include any third-party payer reimbursement.
computation_calculations: (Total out-of-pocket health expenditure in USD adjusted for purchasing power parity (PPP)) / (Total population)
other_info: See the linked data source for other relevant measures, including out-of-pocket expenditure per capita in current USD and out-of-pocket expenditure as a percentage of current health expenditure.
comments_limitations: This indicator is a proxy and does not directly measure the distribution of out-of-pocket health expenditure or its financial impact on households. Limited information on catastrophic health expenditure in Rwanda at the 10% and 25% thresholds can be found on the World Health Organization (WHO) [Global Health Observatory](https://www.who.int/data/gho/data/themes/topics/indicator-groups/indicator-group-details/GHO/catastrophic-out-of-pocket-health-spending-sdg-indicator-3-8-2-).
indicator_name: Proportion of population with positive out-of-pocket household expenditures on health exceeding 40 per cent of household discretionary budget
target_name: Achieve universal health coverage, including financial risk protection, access to quality essential health-care services and access to safe, effective, quality and affordable essential medicines and vaccines for all
indicator_definintion: Proportion of the population with positive out-of-pocket household expenditure on health exceeding 40% of household discretionary budget. The discretionary household budget is defined as total household consumption expenditure or income minus the societal poverty line (SPL). Using 2017 purchasing power parities (PPPs), the SPL corresponds to whichever is greater: $2.15 (the international poverty line) or $1.15 + 50% of median household consumption expenditure or income, excluding out-of-pocket household expenditure on health. All amounts are measured on a per capita daily basis.
